subject: Follow-up: PII handling for prompts/outputs (BrightPath)
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@brightpathhealth.com>, John Patel <john.patel@brightpathhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Feb 2028 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: PII handling for prompts/outputs (BrightPath)

Hi Sarah / John —

Thanks again for taking the time today — quick recap and next steps on the PII / data-handling items we discussed during the demo: 

1) What Redwood stores by default
- For our hosted API, we persist request metadata and prompt/output logs for up to 30 days by default for debugging and abuse detection.
- Prompts/outputs are accessible to authorized support/engineering for troubleshooting during that retention window.

2) Options to avoid storage
- We offer a "no-logging" flag customers can enable on requests which prevents long-term storage of prompts/outputs (only ephemeral in-memory processing).
- For Dedicated and Private deployments we can enable configurations that avoid control-plane logging entirely.

3) Residency & encryption
- Hosted logs are stored in the region you select (we recommended us-east-1 for your account); data at rest is encrypted with AES-256 and keys are managed via our KMS with customer-managed key options for Dedicated/Private.

4) Training / model use
- We do not use customer prompts/outputs from Dedicated or Private deployments to train models. For hosted API, customer data is not used for training by default — we can add contract language to make this explicit for BrightPath.

5) Next steps
- I've looped in Neha from our security team to provide a concise written confirmation with retention windows and controls (see her note below).
- I attached a short summary doc (Redwood_PII_Data_Retention_Summary.pdf) that outlines the defaults and configuration choices.
- If this looks right, can we schedule a 30-min follow-up with your security/compliance team next week?

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@brightpathhealth.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: PII handling for prompts/outputs (BrightPath)

Hi Rishi —

Appreciate the recap. A few clarifying Qs from our security and compliance reviewers: 

- When you say "persist" prompts/outputs for 30 days, does that include full output text and the original prompt (i.e., raw user PII)?
- Where exactly are those logs stored (cloud provider / region)? Are they accessible to Redwood support engineers by default?
- Is there an option to ensure prompts/outputs are never written to disk (ephemeral-only)?
- For hosted API customers, can you contractually guarantee that data will not be used to train models?
- Do you have a SOC 2 / HIPAA stance and a BAA available?

If Neha can confirm the exact default retention and provide the wording we can share with our legal team, that would be great. Thanks —

Sarah Lee
Head of Security & Compliance | BrightPath Health
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@brightpathhealth.com>, John Patel <john.patel@brightpathhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Feb 2028 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: PII handling for prompts/outputs (BrightPath)

Hi all —

Below are concise answers to Sarah's questions. Please consider this a technical confirmation; we can formalize language for contracts/BAAs if needed.

1) What is stored by default?
- Hosted API (default): We retain request and response payloads (including prompt and generated output) for up to 30 days. This retention is for debugging, abuse detection, and forensic purposes.

2) Storage location and access
- Hosted logs are stored in the customer-selected region (BrightPath account defaulted to us-east-1 in our system). Storage is on our cloud provider's managed storage in that region.
- Access: Support and engineering can access logs during the retention window for troubleshooting; access is audited and role-restricted.

3) Ephemeral-only / no-disk options
- No-logging flag: Both hosted and Dedicated APIs support a request-level flag to prevent storage of prompt/outputs beyond ephemeral processing. When enabled, prompts/outputs are processed in-memory and not written to persistent logs.
- Dedicated & Private: For Dedicated deployments we can configure the control plane to avoid storing prompt/output payloads. For Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments, customer data never leaves the customer environment unless explicitly configured to do so.

4) Use for training
- We do not use customer prompts/outputs from Dedicated or Private deployments to train our models. For hosted API, customer data is not used for training by default; if BrightPath requires explicit contractual prohibition, we can add a clause to the agreement.

5) Encryption, KMS, and keys
- Transit: TLS 1.2+/TLS 1.3 for all API traffic.
- At rest: AES-256.
- Key management: Default Redwood-managed keys; customer-managed keys (CMK) are available for Dedicated and Private deployments.

6) Compliance & BAAs
- We are SOC 2 Type II compliant (report available on request). For HIPAA/BAA: We can enter into a BAA for covered use cases; we'll route this through Legal.

Retention windows & audit logs can be adjusted per contract. I've attached a short summary (Redwood_PII_Data_Retention_Summary.pdf) and included a one-page table in the attachment with default windows and opt-out mechanisms.

Happy to join the call with BrightPath's security team.

— Neha Kapoor
Sr. Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
